description:
Your pension is invested in something. You chose a number — how much goes in. You almost certainly never chose where it goes.

That is the default fund, and most people never move it. It buys an index: the largest listed companies, by size, automatically. Nobody screens it — that is the entire point of it.

So look at what the basket holds. Banks and insurers, one of the biggest slices in it. Alcohol. Gambling. Tobacco. Weapons. Not by accident — by construction.

And the banks are the sharp part. A bank's product is not a service. It is interest. Own the bank, own the income.

Then the part almost nobody knows: your fund is built to change as you age. They call it lifestyling, or a glide path. It sounds like safety. The closer you get to retiring, the more it sells shares and buys bonds — and a bond is a loan. You are lending money, at interest. The machine moves you deeper into it as you get older. Automatically, quietly, as a feature you were never shown.

TWO MINUTES. THREE STEPS.
1. Log in. Find the name of your fund. If it says default, balanced, or a retirement year — that is the basket.
2. Search that fund's largest holdings. You will recognise the banks immediately.
3. Open the full fund list. Look for a sharia or Islamic option. Most workplace schemes have one now, and switching is usually free.

Same contributions. Same employer match. Different basket.

You were opted in by default. Default is still a choice — somebody else just made it for you.
